quickAnswerHtml: La Voi (La Voi Pattaya) is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Chon Buri, in the Jomtien–Nong Prue area of Pattaya, with a budget of around THB 70–120 — mostly walk-in, queue at the door

blocks.html:
In a city where most people think first of seafood and beachfront restaurants, the fact that a beef-noodle shop on Chaiyaphruek Road has picked up a Bib Gourmand from the MICHELIN Guide Thailand two years running (2025 and 2026) says something clear — La Voi doesn't sell ordinary beef noodles, it sells "premium beef noodles," made from high-grade beef simmered and stewed until the broth turns rich and deep. It's also a halal restaurant, and in the Jomtien–Nong Prue area, which sees Muslim travelers from the Middle East and Malaysia year-round, having a beef restaurant of this quality that everyone can actually eat at is genuinely hard to find.

What MICHELIN saw in this restaurant is a seriousness about a single core ingredient: beef. The whole menu revolves around it, from the rich beef-noodle soup that's the restaurant's signature dish, to the mixed beef gao lao (noodle-free beef soup) for anyone who wants beef without the noodles, to boiled beef with dipping sauce that shows off the meat's quality in the most straightforward way possible since there's nothing else to hide behind, all the way to La Voi rice, the restaurant's own specialty dish at THB 150. And if there's a group of you, the bai phai hot pot at THB 385 is the best-value answer for a table that wants to try several cuts of beef at once. What makes this restaurant likeable is the price — noodles start at just THB 70–120 a bowl, despite using beef that's genuinely simmered with care, which matches the whole point of a Bib Gourmand award exactly: delicious and good value, not delicious but expensive.

The location also tells another side of Pattaya that passing tourists tend to overlook. The stretch of Chaiyaphruek Road heading toward Jomtien Beach is where actual Pattaya locals live and eat, not a walking-street zone where prices are set for tourists. The restaurant sits near Seven Condo, easy to find, and the fact that a place like this shows up on a MICHELIN list is a kind of confirmation that Pattaya's genuinely good food is scattered along side streets just like this one. Anyone driving back into town from Jomtien Beach, or staying in a condo around Nong Prue, should carve out time for a lunch stop here at least once — and you'll understand why MICHELIN handed it the award again for a second year running.

blocks.name: La Voi (La Voi Pattaya)
blocks.descHtml:
La Voi is on Chaiyaphruek Road, on the side heading toward Jomtien Beach — easy to spot near Seven Condo, in Pattaya's Jomtien–Nong Prue area. The restaurant is open Tuesday–Friday 09:00–18:00, Saturday–Sunday 09:00–16:30, and closed every Monday — remember the closing day, since plenty of people miss it. It's walk-in only, with no table booking system; if you want to check ahead whether it's open or whether dishes have sold out, call 097-161-5566.

On budget: noodles and gao lao run about THB 70–120 a bowl, La Voi rice is THB 150, and the bai phai hot pot for sharing across the table is THB 385. On average, budget around THB 150–300 per person for a full meal. The restaurant is halal, so Muslim friends can eat here without worry, and the dress code is casual — no need to overthink it. The best time to go is lunch, since the restaurant closes fairly early (6pm on weekdays, 4:30pm on weekends) — don't plan on dinner here. Anyone driving from central Pattaya or Jomtien Beach is only a few minutes away, making it a perfect stop before or after a swim at Jomtien.
